chapter: Ellington, the South, bebop and radio
title: Musicians learning in Army bands and the G.I. Bill
summary: Many musicians learned more by joining Army bands and music schools during the war and under the G.I. Bill.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well, there were quite a few good musicians around. Teddy and Roy, I played with them in 1930 -- '29 and '30. So I know they were good! We had a good band. But the guys around them days were able to sit in, oh, up to around '35 or '36, '37 maybe...maybe clear up to '40... Then the War started, and a number of guys left and (?). I guess a lot of them learned a lot by going into the Army and getting...
Bands, getting into the bands. They learned quite a bit.
Then they got more formal schooling and stuff.
Yeah. I mean, they got in, they had a chance to go to school, the music schools in the Army, and really get with it. That G.I., what-do-you-call-it...?
That was another element, I guess, that made a difference. But like, when you first heard Charlie Parker and Dizzy... I don't know when that was. It was probably around...
